description: cypher dialect version neo4j 3.5 old syntax
text: Write Neo4j 3.5 Cypher only: no EXISTS { }, COUNT { } or CALL { } subqueries.
Write every relationship in the direction given in the schema: (source)-[:TYPE]->(target).

description: find a named entity: a specific disease, compound, drug or gene given by its name
text: Look an entity up by exact name with a property map, e.g. (d:Disease {name: '...'}); do not use CONTAINS or regular expressions unless asked.

description: which entities are directly related to a given entity: treats, binds, causes, presents
text: For a direct relation use one MATCH pattern with one relationship type and RETURN DISTINCT the name of the entity asked for.

description: entities connected through a shared intermediate entity, such as genes shared by a compound and a disease
text: For multi-step questions chain patterns through the shared node, e.g. (a)-[:R1]->(shared)<-[:R2]-(b), instead of two unrelated MATCH clauses.

description: how many, number of, count of shared or distinct items
text: Count with count(DISTINCT x) and give the result an alias, e.g. count(DISTINCT g) AS shared_genes.

description: top N, the most, highest, ranking, best five, order results
text: For top-N questions use ORDER BY <count> DESC, then name ASC as a tie-break, then LIMIT N with exactly the N asked for.

description: but not, excluding, not known to, without an existing relationship
text: To exclude entities that already have a relationship use a pattern predicate: WHERE NOT (a)-[:TYPE]->(b), with both variables bound earlier in the query.

description: at least, more than, threshold on a count or aggregate
text: To filter on an aggregate, compute it in WITH and filter after it: WITH a, count(DISTINCT b) AS n WHERE n >= 2.

description: name spelling, capital letters, upper or lower case of a name
text: Names are case-sensitive; if the spelling may differ compare with toLower(n.name) = toLower('...').

description: return name and another value, list columns, output fields
text: Return only the columns the question asks for, each with an explicit alias (AS name).
